summary: Built and registered the lost-decision probe the current discriminator called for: a successor execution whose harness adds a three-voter lost_acknowledged_commit case (demote both peers to leave one voter, snapshot that configuration, promote both peers back to voters, stop everything, restart the former leader, acknowledge one uniquely named commit on it, then bring the other two voters back with the flag disabled and scan every store for that payload before and after the holder rejoins). Local verification before submission: with the flag enabled the restarted instance reconstructed one voter against its log's three, elected itself alone and acknowledged the payload, which afterwards existed on exactly one copy with the other two voters never having received it; with the flag disabled it reconstructed the three-voter configuration and acknowledged nothing ("node is not the leader"). Four comparisons are declared: reconstructed voter count against the log's configuration entry with its control, and the acknowledged commit's durability on a majority of the committed configuration with its control; validation reports a valid update with one experiment created and an execution requested. Incomplete: the receipt is outstanding, so this turn recorded no interpretation, and the probe does not yet show the acknowledged copy being discarded (the holder still carries it after rejoining), so that stronger consequence remains unestablished.
